known_input_issue: Spreadsheet off-diagonals were interpreted as tensor entries. Original Nastran rigid-body mass matrices establish the opposite CONM2 product signs. Use pazy-primary-conm2-* inputs and pazy-loaded-source-audit.json. Numerical results below reproduce the historical inputs only.

discrete_reference.explanation: At one midpoint interval per pair of massive nodes, 30 zero-shear constraints reduce 90 free coordinates to 60, giving 120 first-order finite states. Subdivision adds massless internal coordinates; the refined pencil retains all 90 massive coordinates and has 180 finite states. This is a discretization effect, not a deleted low mode or a continuum-spectrum claim.

limits: Intrinsic axial/torsion K12 is explicitly removed to fit documented ASWING section fields; all remaining constants are mapped exactly.
Full primary stiffness and its projected counterpart are both evaluated by an independent exact linear nodal-mass beam.
The reference axis is .441 chord in the paper and rounded to .44 in the README. No aerodynamic validation is claimed.
Reference K/M have no distributed mass. Original nodal inertia locations and full tensors are retained, including root mass constrained by the clamp.
Primary UM/NAST uses a different finite-element discretization; its coarse frequencies are not assumed to be a continuum reference.
Gravity-free comparisons do not establish loaded/static/experimental validation. Original literal Pazy attachment behavior is still unresolved.

attachment_audit.finding: The public guides identify t as the beam anchor and Cartesian coordinates as the pylon endpoint. They do not specify out-of-domain t behavior; no clamping or extrapolation change was made.

next_steps: Check self-weight equilibrium, gravity-loaded modes and complete static measured curves with these primary properties.
Resolve original .asw attachment semantics using authoritative documentation or controlled ASWING observations.
Reconcile precise test loads, reference-axis/chord geometry, calibration dependence and measurement uncertainty before any physical-validation pass.
Complete remaining aerodynamic/aeroelastic and other family comparisons; this study does not validate flutter or time response.
